title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram

content.problemStatement:
You're given an array of integers representing the heights of bars in a
histogram, each bar one unit wide and placed side by side.

**Return the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed using
only contiguous bars, where the rectangle's height is limited by the
shortest bar it spans.**
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: bars at indices 2 and 3 (heights 5 and 6) form a rectangle of height 5 and width 2, area 10
either a single bar of height 4 and width 1 (area 4), or both bars at height 2 and width 2 (also area 4)
all four bars together form a rectangle of height 1 and width 4

code.Python3:
# Time:  O(n)
# Space: O(n)

class Solution(object):
    def largestRectangleArea(self, heights):
        """
        :type heights: List[int]
        :rtype: int
        """
        stk, result = [-1], 0
        for i in range(len(heights)+1):
            while stk[-1] != -1 and (i == len(heights) or heights[stk[-1]] >= heights[i]):
                result = max(result, heights[stk.pop()]*((i-1)-stk[-1]))
            stk.append(i) 
        return result
